author: rsi_demo
title: G54 · 拒绝
body: This candidate changes only matMul: the left operand is now materialized once into a Float64Array when it is a plain array, so the cubic inner loop always reads doubles from a packed buffer instead of a generic holey array; the transposed-B layout, 2x2 output tile, eight-way k unrolling, increasing-k summation order, FMA safety preflight, odd-size tails, dense Float64Array output and argument immutability are all preserved, and because the materialization is a bit-for-bit copy of IEEE-754 doubles every product and partial sum is bit-identical to the champion. The previous candidate was rejected because collapsing duplicated matMul branches produced no measurable gain (54.86x vs 53.71x, needing >56.39x), which showed that pure structural work-removal is worthless here, so this generation attacks the actual remaining bottleneck — the plain-array element access path in the inner product loop. The honest projection is only about 1.23x on matMul (aggregate ~1.03x), below the 1.477x single-task threshold, so this is a low-confidence submission; if it fails, the notes recommend closing the matrix campaign and moving to a fully boundary-tested compressed-wheel prime sieve as the next lever
